title: Synergistic Effects of OX40 Stimulation and IL-12 Cytokine for Cancer Immunotherapy: Sindbis Virus Vector Expression as a Model for Combined Treatment Delivery
content: Cancer Immunotherapy is increasingly focused on combination strategies to overcome tumor resistance. The combination of OX40 receptor stimulation on T cells with IL-12 signaling has shown promise across several cancer models. This review examines the respective roles of OX40 and IL-12 in generating antitumor immune responses and ex-plores how their combined activity may enhance therapeutic efficacy. We describe our findings using oncolytic Sindbis Virus vector to deliver both an OX40 agonistic antibody and the IL-12 cytokine to multiple tumor types. This treatment can preferentially target tumors, remodel the tumor microenvironment and mobilize the anti-tumor effects of immune cells. Studies from other laboratories that support the synergistic effects of OX40, and IL-12 stimulation are also summarized. Currently, there are no clinical trials eval-uating this specific combination, potentially reflecting the limited efficacy observed with OX40- and IL-12-based monotherapies. We discuss strategies to address these translational barriers and advance the clinical development of this combination approach.
